extracted.intended_audience: comics creators, publishers, industry professionals, Comic‑Con attendees, and comics fans
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement of the 2025 Will Eisner Comic Industry Awards: lists nominees and winners across categories, describes eligibility and voting procedures, and provides Hall of Fame and special‑award details. Includes ceremony logistics and sponsor information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility period for nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: The nominations are for works published between January 1 and December 31, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All categories apply to works published within that calendar year (2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting process (two-step online)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting for the awards is being held online using a two-step process. The first step is for prospective voters to apply at https://cci.tiny.us/2025Eisners. After filling out the form, eligible voters will be invited to go to the ballot and cast their votes. Those who previously registered will automatically be invited to fill out the new ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New voters must have registered by May 29 to be invited to the ballot; the deadline for voting is June 5. Questions about the voting process should be sent to the Eisner Awards administrator, Jackie Estrada at jackie@comic-con.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: General voter eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: All professionals in the comic book industry are eligible to vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professionals include creators, publishers, editors, historians, educators, librarians, and retail store owners/managers (see more specific lists for Hall of Fame).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges panel selects nominees
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations were chosen by a blue‑ribbon panel of judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2025 Eisner Awards judging panel consists of editor/journalist/publisher Robert V. Conte, graphic novel librarian Kacy Helwick, review editor Meg Lemke, comics retailer Eitan Manhoff, and educator Rocco Versaci.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will Eisner Hall of Fame nomination and selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hall of Fame judges choose 18 nominees; voters then select 6 inductees from those nominees. Trophies are presented for 21 judges’ choices and 6 inductees chosen by voters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting for the Hall of Fame is held online via a two‑step process; prospective voters apply at the same application link. The Hall of Fame judging panel consists of Dr. William Foster, Michael T. Gilbert, Karen Green, Alonso Nuñez, Jim Thompson, and Maggie Thompson. Deadline for Hall of Fame voting is March 20; voters must have registered by March 13 to be invited to the ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will Eisner Spirit of Comics Retailer Award (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given to a store that has done an outstanding job of supporting the comics art medium both in the community and within the industry at large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award recognizes retail stores for community and industry‑level support of comics; presented by Joe Ferrara in 2025 (winner: Akira Comics of Madrid, Spain).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bob Clampett Humanitarian Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual humanitarian award presented since 1984 (presented by Bob’s daughter Ruth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given for humanitarian contributions related to comics (2025 recipient: Mad Cave Studios for the L.A. Strong charity comic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Russ Manning Promising Newcomer Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual award recognizing a promising newcomer in the field (handed out since 1982).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented by past Russ Manning assistant and related presenters; 2025 recipient: Richard Blake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill Finger Award for Excellence in Comic Book Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual award recognizing excellence in comic book writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in conjunction with the Eisners; 2025 recipients: Don Glut and Sheldon Mayer. Major sponsor for the Finger Award is DC Comics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Short Story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the Eisner Award categories (winners/nominees listed for 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Single Issue/One‑Shot
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes a single issue or one‑shot publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Continuing Series
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes an ongoing series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Limited Series
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes a series with a planned limited run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best New Series
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes a series debuting within the eligibility period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Publication for Early Readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Category title: Best Publication for Early Readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes publications aimed at very young readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Publication for Kids
rubrics_metrics.description: Category title: Best Publication for Kids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes publications intended for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Publication for Teens
rubrics_metrics.description: Category title: Best Publication for Teens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes publications targeted at teen readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Humor Publication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes publications primarily in the humor genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Anthology
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes collections/anthologies of multiple creators or stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Reality‑Based Work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes nonfiction or reality‑based comics and graphic narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Graphic Memoir
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes memoirs in graphic form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Graphic Album—New
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes newly published graphic albums (original works).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Graphic Album—Reprint
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes reprints/reissued graphic albums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Adaptation from Another Medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Category title: Best Adaptation from Another Medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes works adapted from non‑comics source material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best U.S. Edition of International Material
rubrics_metrics.description: Category title: Best U.S. Edition of International Material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes U.S. editions/translations of international comics/graphic novels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best U.S. Edition of International Material—Asia
rubrics_metrics.description: Category title: Best U.S. Edition of International Material—Asia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes U.S. editions/translations of Asian comics/manga.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Archival Collection/Project—Strips
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes archival projects focused on newspaper/comic strips and related early works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Archival Collection/Project—Comic Books
rubrics_metrics.description: Category title: Best Archival Collection/Project—Comic Books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes archival recollections/projects of comic book material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Comics‑Related Periodical/Journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes periodicals and journalism covering comics (magazines, websites, journals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Comics‑Related Book
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes books about comics (history, criticism, biographies, reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Academic/Scholarly Work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes academic scholarship on comics (edited volumes, monographs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Publication Design
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes excellence in the design and production of comics publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Digital Comic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes comics published digitally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Webcomic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes serialized comics published on the web.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Writer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes excellence in writing for comics across eligible works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Writer/Artist
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes creators who both write and draw their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Penciller/Inker or Penciller/Inker Team
rubrics_metrics.description: Category title: Best Penciller/Inker or Penciller/Inker Team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes excellence in pencils and inks, individually or as a team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Painter/Multimedia Artist
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes creators using painting or multimedia techniques in comics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Cover Artist
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes excellence in cover art across eligible titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Coloring
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes excellence in color work for comics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Lettering
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes excellence in lettering and typographic design for comics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremony attendance & logistical eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance at the Eisner Awards event is free to all Comic‑Con members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendees must bring their convention badge to be admitted and their I.D. to purchase alcoholic beverages; advance seating for VIPs begins at 7:00; doors open at 7:45 and ceremony begins at 8:00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship and presentation roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Major, principal, supporting, and afterparty sponsors are listed for the awards, and specific presenters/hosts are named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors and presenters help shape the ceremony but are not eligibility criteria; they include Lunar Distribution (major sponsor), Comic Shop Assistant, Comixology Originals, mycomicshop.com, Pan‑Universal Galactic Worldwide, and others.
